questions.q: Why can you compare the sizes of the logistic regression coefficients directly in this project?
options: Logistic regression always produces comparable coefficients
The numeric features were standardized, so each coefficient is the change in log-odds per one standard deviation
Coefficients are always between -1 and 1
Because the model was trained on the test set
questions.explain: Standardizing puts numeric inputs on a common scale. Without it, a feature measured in days and one measured in dollars would have incomparable coefficients.

options: How much the model's score drops when one feature's values are shuffled on held-out data
How many times the feature appears in the training set
The p-value of the coefficient
The correlation between the feature and the label
questions.explain: Shuffling breaks the feature's link to the outcome. A larger drop in average precision means the model relied on that feature more.

questions.q: Tenure had a positive coefficient (longer tenure, more churn). What did the follow-up experiment show?
options: Tenure should be removed because it contradicts common sense
Loyalty causes churn
Tenure correlates 0.70 with the cumulative count of late or refunded orders, and adding that count improved cross-validated AP in 14 of 15 folds, supporting (not proving) that tenure was a stand-in
Nothing; the experiment was inconclusive
questions.explain: The result supports the hypothesis that tenure was standing in for accumulated bad deliveries. It is association, not proof of cause, and the new feature belongs in a version 2 checked on fresh data.

questions.q: Why was the bad-order count experiment run with cross-validation on training data only, and not evaluated on the test set?
options: Test sets cannot be used with new features
The test set is already spent; using it again to judge a feature found after looking would make the reported test result unreliable
Cross-validation is always more accurate than a test set
The count was not available for test customers
questions.explain: The test result was reported once in lesson 10. Anything chosen using it afterwards would no longer be an independent estimate. A real version 2 needs fresh data such as the next snapshot.

questions.q: In the SHAP explanation for customer 3592 (predicted 0.279, base value 0.134), what do the SHAP values add up to?
options: The customer's tenure in days
Zero
The difference, in log-odds, between the customer's prediction and the base value
The number of features
questions.explain: SHAP contributions start from the base value and add up, in log-odds, to that customer's prediction. Positive values raise risk, negative values lower it.
